articleSummary: Half-cut watermelon slices may harbor pathogenic bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Listeria monocytogenes. articleHeadline: 手足口病高发季，人二倍体细胞与Vero细胞疫苗究竟怎么选？
articleSummary: HFMD peaks in summer 2026, with enterovirus 71 (EV71) driving severe cases; timely vaccination of young children is key. EV71 vaccines use two substrates: human diploid cells (HDC) and Vero cells. WHO guidelines treat both platforms as equivalent; no preferred option. Real-world data from Hebei Province, China (2019–2023) show adverse-event rates around 14.21 per 100,000 doses for EV71-Vero and EV71-H2, with no significant difference. In Vero-cell vaccines, Sinovac’s EV71-Vero shows low adverse events: a 2018 multicenter study found overall rates of 4.8% vs 5.1% for HDC vaccines; among ages 24–35 months, 2.5% vs 5.3% (p<0.001). Immunogenicity indicates onset within 10 days; overall protection against HFMD is 94.6% and 100% against severe disease. Durability exceeds 5 years, with seropositivity 97.17% at 2 months and 94.34% at 64 months. For 6–71 months olds, timely vaccination at licensed clinics—regardless of platform—is the rational choice.

articleHeadline: 5500年前，这种致命疾病曾大规模夺走人类生命 -- 新闻 -- 科学网
articleSummary: Ancient plague outbreaks date back 5500 years in eastern Siberia near Lake Baikal among hunter-gatherers, according to a Nature study. Researchers sequenced dental-derived Yersinia pestis DNA from 46 burials at two sites; 18 individuals tested positive (about 39–40%), among the earliest and with high virulence. Radiocarbon dating shows a sharp, short-lived fatal wave, with close relatives (siblings, parents, children) dying and buried together, indicating a large infectious disease outbreak. The team linked the ancient pathogen to Marmota (marmots) exposure; the evidence supports transmission from wild rodents (not flea-mediated) to humans, predating farming and urbanization. The results corroborate a hypothesis that plague originated in Central/Northeast Asia and spread across Eurasia via rodent populations. This ancient outbreak demonstrates plague’s devastating lethality in early human communities, particularly among children.

articleSummary: As of June 24, 2026, rhinovirus infections are rising in Changsha, Hunan Province, China. Pediatricians report many children with common cold symptoms—nasal congestion, runny nose, and cough. Health authorities warn against self-medication: there is no targeted antiviral for rhinovirus, antibiotics do not treat viruses, and combining multiple cold medicines can risk liver or kidney injury. Oseltamivir and other anti-flu drugs are ineffective against rhinovirus. Mild cases should be managed with home, symptomatic care; antibiotics should only be used under physician guidance if a bacterial infection is suspected or confirmed. Watch for complications such as otitis media, bronchitis, and acute asthma exacerbations, especially in infants and immunocompromised children. Rhinovirus spreads via droplets and close contact; prevention includes regular handwashing, avoiding crowded, poorly ventilated places, nasal saline rinses, adequate fluids, and rest. Seek medical care for persistent cough, fever, wheeze, or rapid breathing.

articleSummary: Dengue Fever, spread by Aedes mosquitoes in stagnant water, occurs during the monsoon; no antivirals are available; management centers on hydration, rest, fever control, and platelet monitoring in severe cases. articleHeadline: UNFPA Ebola Outbreak - Democratic Republic of the Congo Appeal (June - November 2026)
articleSummary: As of 24 June 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo is confronting a rapidly evolving Ebola outbreak in Ituri Province and neighboring North and South Kivu, amid persistent conflict, large-scale displacement, attacks on health facilities, and constrained humanitarian access. articleSummary: Measles outbreaks persist in Vietnam. articleSummary: Summer rise in meningococcal disease (Neisseria meningitidis) among children, especially under age 5, driven by hot, humid conditions and increased social contacts. Transmission occurs mainly via droplets; asymptomatic carriers can spread the bacteria. Classic onset includes high fever, severe headache, nausea/vomiting, and neck stiffness, with rapid progression to septic shock and multi-organ failure; death can occur within 24 hours if untreated. Global mortality can reach about 50% without timely treatment, and survivors may suffer long-term sequelae such as deafness or neurological impairment. WHO identifies vaccination as the most effective prevention. Serogroups A, B, C, W, X, Y account for most cases globally; a quadrivalent vaccine against A, C, Y, W is available for children from 9 months. Parents should review immunization history and seek reputable clinics. In Vietnam, Long Chau Pharmacy and Vaccination System reports rising demand and maintains vaccine supply and cold-chain integrity (GSP) with 24/7 monitoring. Additional measures include hygiene, handwashing, covering coughs, ventilation, and adequate nutrition and rest.
notes: 記事は髄膜炎菌病の季節的上昇傾向と予防接種の重要性について保健専門家による啓発内容。具体的な発症者数、死亡例、医療施設の対応状況に関する定量的データが提供されていないため、深刻度の判定には情報が限定的。ただしベトナムでの需要増加とワクチン供給体制の整備状況について触れられており、保健当局の認識があることが示唆される。

articleSummary: Vietnam, Haiphong resident, 77-year-old man treated at Hai Duong Tropical Diseases Hospital was found to be co-infected with Fasciola gigantica (giant liver fluke) and Strongyloides stercoralis. He suffered long-standing generalized itching, multiple nodular skin lesions, and scratching-induced secondary bacterial skin infection. Laboratory tests confirmed simultaneous infection with both parasites. After treatment, his condition markedly improved; one month later, itching diminished, skin lesions improved, and overall health stabilized. Clinicians warned that dual parasitic infections can be missed until symptoms persist or complications arise, recommending evaluation for unexplained pruritus, recurrent rashes, or GI symptoms. Prevention guidance: Fasciola gigantica exposure occurs via contaminated water or aquatic greens (e.g., watercress, water parsley) that should be washed and cooked; Strongyloides exposure occurs when skin-penetrating soil larvae contact the skin, so wear gloves and closed-toe footwear in farming or soil work and avoid barefoot exposure in contaminated environments.

articleHeadline: Development of an immunochromatographic lateral flow assay for the rapid detection of all known orthoebolavirus glycoproteins - npj Viruses
articleSummary: An immunochromatographic lateral flow rapid diagnostic test (ILF-RDT) detects glycoproteins from all known orthoebolaviruses—Ebola, Sudan, and Bundibugyo—addressing diagnostic gaps in Sub-Saharan Africa where outbreaks occur. The test uses novel broadly cross-reactive monoclonal antibodies targeting viral GP, including secreted GP, in a non-competitive binding format. It detects both recombinant GP and authentic virus across substrates, including samples spiked with human blood and blood from experimentally infected animals. In nonhuman primate samples, Ebola virus was detectable at 4 days post-infection, before severe symptoms appear. The ILF-RDT complements RT-qPCR and other molecular tests, is suitable for point-of-care use in resource-limited settings, and could significantly aid management and mitigation of orthoebolavirus outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.

articleSummary: India's monsoon drives a wave of gut infections as high humidity, standing water, and temperature swings foster growth and spread of bacteria, viruses and parasites. articleSummary: On June 24, 2026, Dong Nai authorities culled 1,942 pigs at a contract farm in Trà Cổ 11, Tan Phú Ward, Dong Nai City after African swine fever (ASF) was confirmed. articleHeadline: In DRC, misinformation and lack of supplies are making the Ebola outbreak harder to contain - CARE
articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is hampered by misinformation and shortages of PPE and testing supplies. CARE, active for over 20 years and coordinating with the Ministry of Health since the outbreak began, operates in 22 health zones across Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu, training health workers, tracking cases, sharing reliable information, and distributing hygiene kits (soap, hand sanitizer) and PPE such as gloves and gowns. Funding cuts constrain response, with staffing shortages limiting outreach, early detection, case reporting, and dissemination of accurate information. Lab equipment and testing supplies are also running low. CARE’s presence has built community trust, enabling culturally appropriate messaging via community dialogue, radio, mobile outreach, and local leaders to counter rumors. As of publication, the response covers about 220,000 people; with funding, it could reach 1 million through hygiene-kit distributions to 20,000 households, expanded communications, and stronger support for local health facilities.

WHO noted symptom overlap with malaria and typhoid, underscoring the need for early detection. articleHeadline: Explainer: Critical constraints risk further Ebola spread as cases surpass 1,000
articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri province) and Uganda surpasses 1,000 cases, with 1,094 cases and 277 deaths in DRC as of June 24, 2026; 387 patients are in isolation or treatment and 115 recovered. Uganda reports 20 cases and 2 deaths. Ituri accounts for over 90% of the total burden; the outbreak strains health systems amid conflict, displacement, and attacks on facilities, with more than 900,000 displaced. A licensed vaccine or therapeutic for the Bundibugyo strain is unavailable, preventing ring vaccination; containment relies on early detection, isolation, contact tracing (only about 12% of contacts under active follow-up), safe burials, infection prevention, and coordination. Burial capacity is severely insufficient (84 personnel vs 540 needed). Lab testing improved to same-day 24-hour turnaround; cross-border movement and a $518 million six-month continental response plan by Africa CDC and WHO remains underfunded, underscoring need for global solidarity.

articleSummary: Measles is a highly contagious disease in Vietnam. From January 1 to June 10, 2026, the National Children's Hospital recorded 740 cases, averaging about 30 per week. One infected person can spread to 12–18 others when community immunity is insufficient; herd immunity ≥95% is needed to curb outbreaks. Most cases occur in children who have incomplete or missing vaccinations. Many patients had visited northern-area healthcare facilities before transfer, underscoring transmission in crowded settings, especially among unvaccinated youngsters. Vaccines schedule: first dose at 9–12 months, second at 15–18 months, and a booster at 4–6 years; in high-risk periods, vaccination may begin at 6 months per MOH/WHO guidance. Vaccines used include measles-only, MR, MMR, and MMRV. Parents of children with prematurity, malnutrition, or chronic illness may hesitate, but such children can be vaccinated safely under medical assessment; full immunization shields individuals and the community from resurgence.

Monsoon conditions—water contamination, flooding, humidity, mosquitoes, and sanitation disruptions—heighten transmission risks, in line with statements from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and WHO, and experts like Dr Aishwarya R.
